title: Metro Tulsa Foot & Ankle Specialists says a cyber incident may have let information be copied
date_note: Date of the practice's own notice; the notice says unusual activity was noticed on or about July 29, 2026.
geo_basis: practice's name and Oklahoma location per Becker's Spine Review; the notice gives no city
summary: Metro Tulsa Foot & Ankle Specialists says in a notice dated October 28 that it became aware of unusual activity in its network on or about July 29, 2026, and that information may have been copied without authorization on July 30. Becker's Spine Review says a ransomware group claimed on Aug. 31 to have the practice's data, citing an Oct. 29 Claim Depot report; the notice does not mention a claim.
plain: A foot and ankle practice in Oklahoma says a cyber incident may have let information be copied without authorization. It says it is notifying people by mail and offering credit monitoring.
exec: A medical practice has told patients that data may have been copied in a cyber incident.
action: Metro Tulsa says it is notifying affected people by mail and offering credit monitoring; use the practice's dedicated line in its notice with questions.
impact: Information may have been copied without authorization, per the practice's notice.

sources.name: Metro Tulsa Foot & Ankle Specialists, notice of data privacy event

validation.note: The practice's own notice, read, states the incident; Becker's Spine Review relays it. The ransomware-group claim appears only in Becker's, citing Claim Depot (a tracker, not read); the notice does not mention it.

review.note: claim not in sources: removed SoulGroup 19 Nov leak-site listing (neither the notice nor Becker's names it); Becker's says an unnamed ransomware group claimed on 31 Aug per Claim Depot, now stated as that; actor, ransomware tag, title and exec fixed; geo_basis notes the notice gives no city
